collection.description: A young villager wonders whether distant peoples remember their dead with songs, silence, flowers or stories.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Preparing a remembrance meal, a young villager wonders whether distant peoples remember their dead with songs, silence, flowers, stories, or nothing at all.

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: An elder suggests that people elsewhere may gather around names and memories just as the village does.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: A parent says some mourn privately and would not welcome a gathering; the preparations become more considerate.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: A storyteller invents a distant tradition of floating lights; the listeners find it moving but acknowledge it is imaginary.

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: The story unsettles a mourner who prefers familiar rites; the group allows the subject to rest.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: A healer proposes that longing for someone absent might be recognizable across cultures.

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: Another villager wonders whether people experience loss in radically different ways; the question stays open.

text_only.reason: "experience" in its everyday sense (what a person has lived through), not a skill gain
